title: Nearly ₹1 Lakh Crore in Bank Deposits Lie Unclaimed in India as RBI Pushes Recovery Drive
excerpt: Unclaimed deposits with RBI's fund have surged to ₹86,917 crore, prompting a nationwide campaign and a centralized portal to help depositors and their heirs reclaim forgotten money.
body:
• Unclaimed bank deposits transferred to RBI's Depositor Education and Awareness Fund have reached ₹86,917 crore, approaching the ₹1 lakh crore mark.
  • The RBI's UDGAM portal, integrated with 30 banks covering ~90% of unclaimed funds, allows depositors and heirs to search for lost deposits online.
  • A nationwide campaign "Apki Poonji, Apka Adhikar" is running through September 2026, with awareness camps in every district.
  • NRIs with dormant accounts in India are among the most affected — the portal offers remote search capability.

India's pile of unclaimed bank deposits is nearing ₹1 lakh crore, with the Finance Ministry telling Parliament that ₹86,917 crore now sits in the Reserve Bank of India's Depositor Education and Awareness (DEA) Fund — money that rightful owners or their heirs have not claimed for over a decade.

The figure, which has been growing steadily, represents savings and current account balances left inoperative for 10 years or more, as well as term deposits unclaimed for 10 years after maturity. Banks are required to transfer such funds to the RBI's DEA Fund, though depositors retain the right to claim the money at any time.

Where the Money Sits

Public sector banks account for the bulk of unclaimed deposits, with ₹60,518 crore transferred as of January 2026. Private sector banks contributed approximately ₹9,600 crore, while foreign banks operating in India added roughly ₹2,275 crore. The total across the banking system stood at over ₹72,000 crore as of early 2026, with the figure subsequently climbing to the reported ₹86,917 crore.

https://x.com/HarshDahiya/status/2087543797299433550

State Bank of India leads among public sector banks in unclaimed deposit amounts, while ICICI Bank tops the list among private lenders.

Beyond banking, unclaimed financial assets extend to insurance (₹8,974 crore) and mutual funds (₹3,749 crore), bringing the total pool of unclaimed financial assets across regulators well above ₹1 lakh crore.

How to Find Unclaimed Deposits

The RBI launched the UDGAM (Unclaimed Deposits – Gateway to Access Information) portal in August 2023, a centralized platform where depositors or their heirs can search for unclaimed funds across 30 banks that cover approximately 90% of all unclaimed deposits.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=pvVUmXocDXg

To search, users register on the portal at udgam.rbi.org.in with their name and mobile number, then search using the account holder's name plus at least one identifier such as PAN, voter ID, driving license, passport number, or date of birth. If a match is found, the portal displays the bank name and a Unique Deposit Reference Number (UDRN).

The portal is a locator, not a withdrawal tool. Claimants must then visit the specific bank branch with their UDRN and required documentation — KYC documents for the account holder, or a death certificate and proof of relationship for legal heirs.

As of April 2026, the portal had registered over 20 lakh users and facilitated 44 lakh searches.

Government's Recovery Campaign

The Department of Financial Services, in coordination with the RBI, SEBI, and IRDAI, launched a nationwide campaign called "Apki Poonji, Apka Adhikar" (Your Money, Your Right). A three-month drive from October to December 2025 resulted in ₹5,777 crore being restored to rightful owners across 22.95 lakh claims settled in camps held across 748 districts.

The campaign is continuing through September 30, 2026, with special awareness camps targeting senior citizens and legal heirs who may need help with documentation.

The Banking Laws Amendment Act, 2025, has also introduced a provision allowing customers to register up to four nominees per bank account — either simultaneously or successively — making it easier for heirs to claim deposits in the future.

What NRIs Should Know

Non-resident Indians who maintained bank accounts before moving abroad are among those most likely to have unclaimed deposits. Accounts left inoperative after emigration are a common source of these funds, particularly savings accounts and fixed deposits that matured while the holder was overseas.

The UDGAM portal is accessible from outside India, allowing NRIs to search for unclaimed deposits remotely. However, completing the claim process may still require visiting the bank branch in person or authorizing someone in India to act on their behalf.

Financial advisors recommend that NRIs regularly check the status of any Indian bank accounts and ensure nominee details are updated to prevent deposits from becoming unclaimed.
nri_angle: NRIs who have left bank accounts dormant in India after moving abroad are among those most likely to have unclaimed deposits; the UDGAM portal and new claim processes offer a way to search for and recover this money remotely.
author: Diaspora Desk
